title: Polynomial-time verifier model
statement: A verifier model consists of a notion of efficiency for option-valued two-input verifiers and a notion of efficiency for Boolean-valued three-input predicates. In the polynomial-time model, an option-valued verifier is efficient exactly when there are languages $V_1,V_0$ in $P$ such that, for every input $x$ and string $r$, it returns true exactly when the pair encoding of $(x,r)$ belongs to $V_1$, and returns false exactly when that encoding belongs to $V_0$; a three-input predicate is efficient exactly when there is a language $V$ in $P$ such that its value on $(x,u,v)$ is true exactly when the nested pair encoding of $(x,u,v)$ belongs to $V$.
hypotheses_covered: Verifier model has an efficiency predicate for option-valued two-input verifiers
Verifier model has an efficiency predicate for Boolean-valued three-input predicates
For option-valued efficiency, existence of $V_1,V_0\in P$
Exact equivalences between true/false outputs and membership of encoded pairs
For three-input efficiency, existence of $V\in P$
Exact equivalence between true output and membership of the nested pair encoding
